mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 9.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a deteriorating labor market that triggers risk-off sentiment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9.0% for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and industrial production indicate a broad-based demand contraction, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 550 and INDPRO < 92.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production, the supply chain disruption risk increases, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors price in higher input costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 92.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in non-farm payrolls over the past 6 months indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises over 6 months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the core CPI rate exceeds 2.5% annually, it signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in retail sales and housing starts indicate a weakening consumer demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenue growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS < 380000 and HOUST < 550, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the context of a slowing GDP growth rate, weak consumer demand leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profit margins face pressure from reduced sales.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 < 13400.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
